body:
A higher bid has put the Australian property group back in focus, but one strategic acquisition remains a sticking point for the investor.

Australian company Ingenia Communities is considering an improved A$2.14 billion buyout offer from US investment firm Warburg Pincus. Shares in Ingenia rose on the exchange after the announcement.

Terms of Warburg Pincus’ new offer

Warburg Pincus is offering A$5.25 per share, almost 4% more than its previous offer of A$5.05 per share, which valued the company at A$2.06 billion. The new price is also 16.7% above the last share price before the announcement.

Warburg Pincus previously made an initial offer of A$4.75 per share, or A$1.94 billion. Ingenia rejected both earlier offers, saying they significantly undervalued the company.

In its new offer, the investor retained a condition requiring Ingenia to abandon its planned A$711 million acquisition of planned residential community developer Peet. Ingenia considers the deal an important part of its strategy.

Board and share price reaction

Ingenia’s board is assessing the revised offer and its terms but has not yet formed a position. The board has not made a recommendation to shareholders on the deal.

Following the news, the company’s shares rose as much as 7.1%, reaching their highest level since late January. Since the start of September, when Ingenia first disclosed that it had received a buyout offer, the shares have gained nearly 30%.
